key_insight: Using the visible forearm as a geometric anchor lets a monocular, head-mounted camera recover absolute camera-space 3D hand pose and shape, resolving depth/scale ambiguity that plagues egocentric RGB methods.
problem_solved: Monocular egocentric hand-pose methods suffer from depth–scale ambiguity and poor generalization across varied head-mounted optics; this paper addresses how to produce absolute, camera-space 3D hand pose and shape from a single wearable RGB camera.
method: Detect and model forearm/wrist geometry visible in the egocentric view to provide a stable scale and orientation anchor for the hand.
Fuse forearm-derived geometric cues with a learned hand-pose/shape estimator to predict absolute (camera-space) 3D joint locations and mesh.
Train with egocentric-aware supervision and geometric consistency losses so the model generalizes across diverse head-mounted camera configurations.
impact: Provides a practical way to produce absolute 3D hand pose and shape from compact, single-camera setups — enabling more accurate, physically grounded interaction for AR/VR, telepresence, and hand-centric manipulation with minimal hardware.

paper_title: EgoForce: Forearm-Guided Camera-Space 3D Hand Pose from a Monocular Egocentric Camera
paper_authors: Christen Millerdurai, Shaoxiang Wang, Yaxu Xie, Vladislav Golyanik, Didier Stricker
